**Allowed origins** are decided in `worker/src/index.ts`, in the `origin` function passed to `cors({...})` (about lines 19–31). It reflects the origin back only if it is one of these:
- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

Anything else, including a request with no `Origin` header, gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The allowed methods are `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`.

**Adding a custom domain:** add another condition to the `if (...)` inside that `origin` function. For example, add `|| origin === 'https://play.example.com'`. Use an exact match, or `endsWith` if you want subdomains too.

Don't put it in an array. The code comment and `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` both say Hono treats array entries as exact strings, so wildcards wouldn't work there.

Matching is by suffix, so `endsWith('.example.com')` also accepts any depth of subdomain. The scheme isn't checked, so `http://` origins would pass as well. An exact `https://...` match is safer.

You may also need to do these outside the CORS code:
- Update the frontend's API base URL so it points at the Worker.
- Attach the domain to the Pages project in Cloudflare. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS.

I read the code but did not check those two items.
